subject: history_social
passage: At Vindolanda, a Roman fort in northern England, archaeologists have recovered hundreds of thin wooden tablets on which soldiers and their families wrote letters, supply lists, and even party invitations nearly two thousand years ago. Wood normally rots quickly in the ground, but these tablets lay in waterlogged soil containing almost no oxygen, which slowed their decay. At most other Roman forts, the soil is dry and well drained, and no such tablets have been found there. The absence of tablets at those other forts therefore ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: indicates that soldiers at those forts wrote on stone instead of on wood.
choices.B: proves that writing was rare among the soldiers stationed at them.
choices.C: shows that the Vindolanda tablets were carried there from other forts.
choices.D: may reflect conditions in the soil rather than how much people there wrote.

explanation.why: The tablets at Vindolanda survived only because unusual soil slowed the decay of the wood. In the dry soil of other forts, any tablets would probably have rotted away, so finding none there does not tell us whether people at those forts wrote less.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text never mentions writing on stone; it gives soil conditions, not a different writing material, as the likely explanation.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This goes too far: tablets at the other forts may simply have rotted in dry soil, so their absence proves nothing about how often people wrote.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says nothing about tablets being moved from one fort to another.
explanation.D: Correct. Because wood rots quickly in dry soil, the missing tablets could be explained by poor preservation rather than by a lack of writing.
